- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment volatility is high (frequent +1.00/-1.00 swings) and news volume is low, model overfits short-term noise; dampen forecast variance by 10–20%.
- When sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If true outcome is consistently above model forecast (e.g., >2% for 5+ days), model underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses long-term trend; if sentiment is trending upward, add 1–2% to forecast; if bearish, subtract 1–2%.
- If news volume is high (≥3.0) and sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overreact; cap forecast deviation at ±2% of recent 7-day average.
